holidays.name: National Mason Jar Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the humble glass jar that holds everything from pickles and jam to overnight oats, craft cocktails, and a suspicious number of hipster candles.
holidays.origin: The date honors the anniversary of the patent John Landis Mason received on November 30, 1858, for his screw-threaded glass jar, which revolutionized home food preservation.
holidays.funFact: Mason's patent expired in the 1870s, which opened the door for many other companies to produce jars, and the Ball brothers eventually became the most famous name in the business.

holidays.name: National Personal Space Day
holidays.description: A day to remind everyone to take a big step back. It encourages respecting other people's bubbles on crowded buses, in elevators, and in lines at the coffee shop.
holidays.origin: An unofficial observance that grew out of social media and etiquette-themed calendars. It is celebrated on November 30 and has been popularized in the United States.
holidays.funFact: Anthropologist Edward T. Hall coined the term 'proxemics' in the 1960s to study how people use space, and he found that comfortable distances vary widely between cultures.

holidays.name: Stay Home Because You're Well Day
holidays.description: A day to give yourself permission to take a break from work or school and stay home, even though you are not sick. Pajamas, blankets, and snacks are encouraged.
holidays.origin: This tongue-in-cheek observance was created by Gil and Jeannie Duncan as a way to promote mental health and rest, and it is celebrated on November 30 each year.
holidays.funFact: It's meant to be the opposite of 'sick day.' It was reportedly created to counter 'presenteeism,' where people go to work when they are unwell and make everyone else sick.

holidays.name: Computer Security Day
holidays.description: A day to change your passwords, update your software, and finally stop using 'password123' for everything. Honor your digital life by locking it down.
holidays.origin: Started in 1988 by the Association for Computing Machinery, shortly after the Morris worm infected thousands of computers in the early internet, to raise awareness of computer security.
holidays.funFact: The Morris worm of 1988 was one of the first major internet worms and infected an estimated 10 percent of the roughly 60,000 computers connected to the internet at the time.

holidays.name: Meet and Greet Day
holidays.description: A day for introducing yourself to strangers, chatting with neighbors, and finally learning the name of the coworker you have been nodding at for three years.
holidays.origin: An unofficial observance that appeared in holiday calendars encouraging people to make new connections, especially at the end of the year before the holiday season gets busy.
holidays.funFact: Handshakes are thought to date back to ancient times, when extending an open hand showed you were not carrying a weapon.
